name: Jieyang Chaoshan International Airport
before:
An airport serving three cities at once: Jieyang, Shantou and Chaozhou in Guangdong. The site was deliberately chosen near the geographic centre of all three, which is why the name matches none of them cleanly and the code SWA comes from Shantou.

It has grown fast. In 2025 it handled 10.229 million passengers, up 18 per cent year on year.

A terminal expansion completed in December 2022 doubled the building by adding a second wing, taking it to 113,000 square metres and lifting design capacity from 4.5 million to 14.5 million passengers a year. There are 26 jetways, but only two are allocated to international flights, with two more dual-use, so international capacity is narrow.

There is an adjacent Jieyang Airport railway station, and a second check-in facility outside Shantou Railway Station, which is useful for a client staying in Shantou.

It opened on 15 December 2011, replacing Shantou Waisha Airport, which closed to commercial flights the same day.
after:
The airport for Jieyang in Guangdong. It sits between three cities, Jieyang, Shantou and Chaozhou.

Traffic is growing fast: in 2025 it handled about 10.2 million passengers, up 18 per cent on 2024.

It has its own railway station, Jieyang Airport.

claims.claim: the airport for Jieyang in Guangdong
claims.inAfter: The airport for Jieyang in Guangdong.
claims.note: CAAC files it under Jieyang (揭阳/潮汕); OurAirports gives the municipality as Jieyang.

sources.quote: is an international airport serving the cities of Jieyang, Shantou and Chaozhou in South Central China's Guangdong province
Row 揭阳/潮汕: passenger rank 41 in China

claims.claim: sits between Jieyang, Shantou and Chaozhou
claims.inAfter: It sits between three cities, Jieyang, Shantou and Chaozhou.
claims.note: Was 'serving three cities at once ... The site was deliberately chosen near the geographic centre of all three'. The coordinates put the airport inside the triangle the three city centres make: 14.1 km east of Jieyang, 16.6 km south west of Chaozhou and 28.3 km north west of Shantou. Why the site was chosen rests on Wikipedia alone, so it is cut.

quote: the site was chosen to be near the geographic center of Jieyang, Shantou, and Chaozhou
serving the cities of Jieyang, Shantou and Chaozhou
Bearing from Shantou to the airport: 321 degrees, which is north west
Bearing from Jieyang to the airport: 85 degrees, which is east
Bearing from Chaozhou to the airport: 227 degrees, which is south west

claims.claim: about 10.2 million passengers in 2025, up 18 per cent
claims.inAfter: in 2025 it handled about 10.2 million passengers, up 18 per cent on 2024.
claims.note: CAAC 10,228,556 (41st in China), up from 8,665,819; Wikipedia gives 10.229 million and 18.0 per cent, from CAAC. 'Growing fast' is kept from the old text's 'It has grown fast', on the strength of the 18 per cent.

sources.quote: 10.229 million passenger movements, representing a year-on-year increases of 15.5% and 18.0% respectively

claims.claim: its own railway station, Jieyang Airport
claims.inAfter: It has its own railway station, Jieyang Airport.
claims.note: China Railway's own station list (12306) has a station named 揭阳机场, Jieyang Airport (code JUA). Wikipedia says it is next to the airport.

sources.quote: The airport is served by the adjacent Jieyang Airport railway station.

claims.wasBefore: An airport serving three cities at once: Jieyang, Shantou and Chaozhou in Guangdong.
claims.why: Reworded: the position between the three cities is kept with the coordinates as the second source. Nothing outside Wikipedia says it serves Shantou and Chaozhou in so many words: the Guangdong airport group's site answers 468 and Shantou's transport bureau 405.

claims.claim: site deliberately chosen near the centre of all three; name matches none of them; code SWA comes from Shantou
claims.wasBefore: The site was deliberately chosen near the geographic centre of all three, which is why the name matches none of them cleanly and the code SWA comes from Shantou.
claims.why: The reason for the site is Wikipedia's alone; 'matches none of them' is not right (the name starts with Jieyang); and no source says where the code SWA comes from.

claims.claim: 2022 terminal expansion: second wing, 113,000 square metres, capacity 4.5 to 14.5 million
claims.wasBefore: A terminal expansion completed in December 2022 doubled the building by adding a second wing, taking it to 113,000 square metres and lifting design capacity from 4.5 million to 14.5 million passengers a year.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The Guangdong airport group's site answers 468, and Guangdong and Jieyang government sites do not connect.

claims.claim: 26 jetways, two international and two dual-use; international capacity narrow
claims.wasBefore: There are 26 jetways, but only two are allocated to international flights, with two more dual-use, so international capacity is narrow.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and the conclusion drawn from it goes with it.

claims.claim: adjacent railway station and a check-in facility at Shantou Railway Station
claims.wasBefore: There is an adjacent Jieyang Airport railway station, and a second check-in facility outside Shantou Railway Station, which is useful for a client staying in Shantou.
claims.why: The railway station is kept, with China Railway's station list as the second source. The Shantou check-in rests on Wikipedia alone: Shantou's transport bureau site answered 405.

claims.claim: opened 15 December 2011, replacing Shantou Waisha, closed to commercial flights the same day
claims.wasBefore: It opened on 15 December 2011, replacing Shantou Waisha Airport, which closed to commercial flights the same day.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone for the date and the switch. OurAirports lists Shantou Waisha with no scheduled service, but gives no date.
